records.explanation: “Honesty” names an abstract quality.

records.stem: Which of the following is a collective noun?
records.explanation: “Team” names a group collectively.

records.stem: What is the plural of “foot”?
records.explanation: “Feet” is the irregular plural of “foot”.

records.stem: What is the plural of “tooth”?
records.explanation: “Tooth” has the irregular plural “teeth”; duplicate distractors have been replaced.

records.stem: Which of the following is a material noun?
records.explanation: “Gold” names a material and is treated as a material noun in traditional grammar.

records.stem: Which word names the quality of being kind in “Kindness is a great virtue”?
records.explanation: “Kindness” is the abstract noun for being kind; “virtue” is also abstract, so the stem is narrowed.

records.stem: What is the feminine gender of “nephew”?
records.explanation: “Niece” is the female counterpart of “nephew”.

records.stem: Which of the following is a countable noun?
records.explanation: Apples can be counted individually, unlike water, milk or sugar as substances.

records.stem: Which of the following is an uncountable noun?
records.explanation: “Water” is normally an uncountable substance noun.

records.stem: What is the plural of “leaf”?
records.explanation: The plural “leaves” changes the final “f” of “leaf” to “ves”.

records.stem: Which personal name is a proper noun in “Ali lives in Lahore”?
records.explanation: “Ali” is a personal proper noun; “Lahore” is also proper but names a place.

records.stem: Which of the following is a possessive noun?
records.explanation: The apostrophe in “boy’s” marks singular possession.

records.stem: Choose the correct comparative degree of “small.”
records.explanation: “Smaller” is the comparative form used to compare two things.

records.stem: Choose the correct superlative degree of “beautiful.”
records.explanation: The longer adjective “beautiful” forms its superlative with “most”.

records.stem: Identify the adjective of quantity: “There is little water in the bottle.”
records.explanation: “Little” indicates the quantity of uncountable water.

records.stem: Choose the correct adjective: “This is the ______ road in our town.”
records.explanation: A comparison with all roads in the town calls for the superlative “narrowest”.

records.stem: Identify the demonstrative adjective: “These books belong to me.”
records.explanation: “These” points to the books and is a demonstrative determiner, traditionally called a demonstrative adjective.

records.stem: What is the approximate density of liquid water at 4°C?
records.explanation: Water reaches approximately 1,000 kg/m³ near 4°C.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of stress?
records.explanation: Stress is force per unit area, measured in N/m² or pascals.

records.stem: A vernier has 10 divisions equal to 9 mm, and one main-scale division is 1 mm. What is its least count?
records.explanation: Least count = 1 mm − 0.9 mm = 0.1 mm for this specified vernier.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of capacitance?
records.explanation: Capacitance is charge per potential difference, measured in farads.

records.stem: What is Newton’s law of universal gravitation for point masses m₁ and m₂ separated by distance r?
records.explanation: Gravitational force is proportional to both masses and inversely proportional to their separation squared.

records.stem: How many SI base units are there?
records.explanation: SI has seven base units, from which derived units are constructed.

records.stem: What is the acceleration of a body moving with constant velocity?
records.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, so constant velocity gives zero acceleration.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of electromotive force (EMF)?
records.explanation: EMF is energy supplied per unit charge, measured in volts.

records.stem: A 10 N force acts at 60° above the horizontal. What is its horizontal component?
records.explanation: The horizontal component is F cos θ = 10 cos 60° = 5 N.

records.stem: Which nautical unit commonly expresses a ship’s speed?
records.explanation: A knot is one nautical mile per hour; specifying a nautical unit excludes other valid speed units.

records.stem: What is the magnitude of centripetal force for mass m moving at speed v in a circle of radius r?
records.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r, so F = ma = mv²/r.

records.stem: A micrometer screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 circular-scale divisions. What is its least count?
records.explanation: Least count = pitch ÷ divisions = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm.

records.stem: Which is a vector quantity?
records.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, unlike the listed scalars.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of energy?
records.explanation: Energy and work are both measured in joules.

records.stem: What is an ideal body whose inter-particle distances remain fixed under applied forces called?
records.explanation: A rigid-body model assumes no deformation or change in internal distances.

records.stem: What is the magnitude of a body’s weight in a gravitational field of strength g?
records.explanation: Weight is gravitational force and equals mass multiplied by gravitational field strength.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of power?
records.explanation: Power is energy transferred per second, measured in watts.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of velocity?
records.explanation: Velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time.

records.stem: What is the magnitude of Coulomb force between point charges q₁ and q₂ separated by r in vacuum?
records.explanation: The magnitude follows the inverse-square electric-force law with Coulomb constant k.

records.stem: If a force F makes angle θ with the positive x-axis, what is its x-component?
records.explanation: The component along the axis from which the angle is measured is F cos θ.

records.stem: What is water’s approximate specific heat capacity near room temperature?
records.explanation: Liquid water needs about 4,200 joules per kilogram for a one-kelvin temperature rise.

records.stem: What is the approximate average centre-to-centre distance between Earth and the Moon?
records.explanation: The Moon’s average orbital distance is approximately 384,400 kilometres and varies through its orbit.

records.stem: Which SI-derived unit is equivalent to kg·m/s for momentum?
records.explanation: One N·s equals one kg·m/s by the definition of the newton.

records.stem: What is the approximate Coulomb constant k in vacuum?
records.explanation: Coulomb’s constant is approximately 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².

records.stem: A cheetah runs at a stated speed of 70 mph. Approximately what is this in km/h?
records.explanation: Using 1 mile ≈ 1.609 km gives 70 × 1.609 ≈ 113 km/h, without assuming a universal maximum speed.

records.stem: According to OpenStax’s reference table, what representative static-friction coefficient is given for glass on glass?
records.explanation: The cited table lists 0.94 for static and 0.40 for kinetic friction; actual surfaces may differ.

records.stem: What is the relationship between wave speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ?
records.explanation: A wave travels one wavelength per cycle, giving v = fλ.

records.stem: What is the approximate gravitational acceleration at Mercury’s surface?
records.explanation: Mercury’s surface gravity is approximately 3.7 m/s².

records.stem: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
records.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per second.

records.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 25 m/s in 20 s. How far does it travel?
records.explanation: For constant acceleration, distance = average speed × time = (0 + 25)/2 × 20 = 250 m.

records.stem: How many vectors can be added successively using the head-to-tail method?
records.explanation: Placing each next vector’s tail at the previous head allows any finite set to be added.

records.stem: Which principle explains the buoyant force supporting a floating body?
records.explanation: The buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid under Archimedes’ principle.

records.stem: Which SI prefix represents 0.000001, or 10⁻⁶?
records.explanation: The prefix micro means one millionth, or 10⁻⁶.

records.stem: According to OpenStax’s reference table, what representative static-friction coefficient is given for steel on steel?
records.explanation: The cited table lists 0.74 for static friction, distinguishing it from kinetic friction.

records.stem: Which scientist is traditionally associated with the Leaning Tower of Pisa falling-body experiment?
records.explanation: The traditional account attributes the demonstration to Galileo, though its historical occurrence is debated.

records.stem: A carbon sample absorbs 710 J when 1 kg warms by 1 K. What specific heat capacity follows from these stated data?
records.explanation: From c = Q/(mΔT), the given data yield 710 J/(kg·K); this replaces an unsupported carbon value.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of frequency?
records.explanation: One hertz is one cycle per second.

records.stem: Who formulated the law of universal gravitation?
records.explanation: Newton formulated the inverse-square law of universal gravitation; earlier thinkers had discussed gravity.

records.stem: Using F = ma with a ≠ 0, what is the expression for mass?
records.explanation: Rearranging Newton’s second law gives mass as force divided by acceleration.

records.stem: Ali runs 100 m in 12 s. What is his average speed?
records.explanation: Average speed = 100/12 ≈ 8.33 m/s.

records.stem: What is the approximate density of platinum near room temperature?
records.explanation: Platinum is a very dense metal, with density approximately 21,450 kg/m³.

records.stem: Brownian motion is an example of which type of motion?
records.explanation: Particles move irregularly because of uneven molecular collisions.

records.stem: In which year was the International System of Units (SI) formally adopted?
records.explanation: The 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures adopted SI in 1960.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of torque?
records.explanation: Torque is force multiplied by perpendicular distance, giving N·m.

records.stem: A 1 kg ball moves at 2 m/s. What is its momentum magnitude?
records.explanation: Momentum p = mv = 1 × 2 = 2 kg·m/s.

records.stem: Which design change generally improves a racing car’s resistance to overturning?
records.explanation: A lower centre of gravity reduces the tendency to topple.

records.stem: Which instrument on a vehicle’s dashboard displays its instantaneous speed?
records.explanation: A speedometer displays speed, while an odometer measures accumulated distance.

records.stem: Which is a vector quantity?
records.explanation: Velocity includes direction as well as speed.

records.stem: What is the approximate universal gravitational constant G?
records.explanation: G is approximately 6.6743 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² and is not the local acceleration g.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of weight?
records.explanation: Weight is a force, so its SI unit is the newton.

records.stem: What is the SI base unit of mass?
records.explanation: Mass is measured in kilograms, whereas weight is measured in newtons.

records.stem: What equatorial gravitational acceleration does NASA JPL list for Jupiter, approximately?
records.explanation: JPL lists approximately 24.79 m/s² for Jupiter’s equatorial gravity; definitions must be specified.

records.stem: Which device helps replace sliding contact with rolling contact to reduce friction?
records.explanation: Ball bearings provide rolling contact, usually reducing resistance compared with sliding.

records.stem: What is Ohm’s law for an ohmic conductor at constant temperature?
records.explanation: Potential difference is current multiplied by resistance under the stated conditions.

records.stem: For a fixed nonzero force and displacement, at which listed angle is signed work W = Fs cos θ minimum?
records.explanation: Cos 180° = −1 gives the most negative work; at 90° work is zero, not the minimum signed value.

records.stem: Which constant-acceleration equation relates final speed v, initial speed u and displacement s?
records.explanation: Eliminating time from the constant-acceleration equations yields v² = u² + 2as.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
records.explanation: One coulomb is the charge transported by one ampere in one second.

records.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular cuboid of length L, width W and height H?
records.explanation: A cuboid’s volume is its base area LW multiplied by height H.

records.stem: Why may someone jumping from a moving bus stumble forward after landing?

options.label: C
options.text: The ground pushes them backward before contact

options.label: D
options.text: Their body retains forward motion due to inertia

records.explanation: The upper body tends to continue moving as contact slows the feet.

records.stem: What can change an object’s state of motion when it is unbalanced?
records.explanation: An unbalanced resultant force produces acceleration.

records.stem: Which substance is commonly used to lubricate sliding metal surfaces?
records.explanation: Oil separates contacting surfaces and usually reduces friction and wear.

records.stem: What upward force holds a 10 kg body stationary when g = 10 m/s² and no other forces act?
records.explanation: Equilibrium requires an upward force equal to weight mg = 100 N.

records.stem: What is the circular orbital speed around a mass M at orbital radius r, neglecting other bodies?
records.explanation: Equating GMm/r² with mv²/r gives v = √(GM/r).

records.stem: What is the approximate specific heat capacity of gold near room temperature?
records.explanation: A representative room-temperature value for gold is approximately 129 J/(kg·K).

records.stem: What is the SI base unit of luminous intensity?
records.explanation: Candela measures luminous intensity; “light” alone does not specify a physical quantity.

records.stem: In a frame rotating with angular speed ω, what is the magnitude of centrifugal force on mass m at radius r?
records.explanation: The apparent centrifugal force in the rotating frame has magnitude mω²r and points outward.

records.stem: Which is a scalar quantity?
records.explanation: Mass has magnitude but no direction.

records.stem: What is the unit of strain?
records.explanation: Strain is change in length divided by original length, so the units cancel.

records.stem: What force opposes relative sliding between contacting surfaces?
records.explanation: Sliding friction acts against the relative motion at contact.

records.stem: What is the named SI unit of pressure?
records.explanation: One pascal equals one newton per square metre; equivalent alternatives are not listed as distractors.

records.stem: What is the approximate specific heat capacity of silver near room temperature?
records.explanation: Silver’s representative specific heat capacity is approximately 235 J/(kg·K).

records.stem: For constant acceleration, which equation gives displacement from initial velocity u over time t?
records.explanation: Integrating velocity u + at over time gives s = ut + ½at².

records.stem: What is the escape of molecules from a liquid’s surface into the gas phase called?
records.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the liquid surface when molecules escape into the surrounding gas.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
records.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in webers, while flux density is measured in teslas.

records.stem: Which equilibrium condition requires the sum of torques about a point to be zero?
records.explanation: Zero resultant torque is the condition for rotational equilibrium.

records.stem: A body weighs 164 N where g = 10 m/s². What is its mass?
What is the work done by a 1 N force moving its point of application 1 m in the force’s direction?
records.explanation: Work W = Fs = 1 × 1 = 1 J.

records.stem: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, what is Boyle’s law?
records.explanation: For an ideal gas at fixed temperature and amount, pressure times volume is constant.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density B?
records.explanation: Magnetic flux density is measured in teslas, equivalent to Wb/m².

records.stem: What is the maximum static friction immediately before slipping called?
records.explanation: Limiting friction is the largest available static-friction force before sliding begins.

records.stem: What is the kinetic energy of mass m moving at nonrelativistic speed v?
records.explanation: Translational kinetic energy is one-half mass multiplied by speed squared.

records.stem: According to OpenStax’s reference table, what representative kinetic-friction coefficient is given for glass on glass?
records.explanation: The cited table distinguishes kinetic friction 0.40 from static friction 0.94.

records.stem: Which law states that total momentum remains constant when external resultant force is zero?
records.explanation: An isolated system has no net external impulse, so its total momentum is conserved.

records.stem: Which named unit is commonly used for optical lens power?
records.explanation: One dioptre is one reciprocal metre, since lens power equals 1/f in metres.

records.stem: What is the approximate density of aluminium near room temperature?
records.explanation: Aluminium’s density is approximately 2.70 g/cm³, or 2,700 kg/m³.

records.stem: An ice block on wood has a stated kinetic-friction coefficient of 0.05 and a normal force of 100 N. What is the friction force?
records.explanation: Using the explicitly given coefficient, f = μN = 0.05 × 100 = 5 N.

records.stem: A 0.15 m spanner is pushed perpendicularly with 200 N. What torque is produced?
records.explanation: Torque τ = rF sin 90° = 0.15 × 200 = 30 N·m.

records.stem: What is the gain in gravitational potential energy when mass m rises through height h in uniform gravity g?
records.explanation: The gain equals weight mg multiplied by vertical height h.

records.stem: What is normal force per unit area called?
records.explanation: Pressure is defined as normal force divided by the area over which it acts.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
records.explanation: Resistance equals potential difference divided by current and is measured in ohms.

records.stem: Which branch of physics studies motion and the forces that cause it?
records.explanation: Mechanics includes the study of motion, forces and their effects.

records.stem: A wood-on-metal contact has a stated friction coefficient of 0.30 and normal force 200 N. What sliding friction is predicted?
records.explanation: With the coefficient supplied rather than assumed universal, f = μN = 0.30 × 200 = 60 N.

records.stem: What is the approximate density of dry air at 20°C and 1 atm?
records.explanation: At these specified conditions dry air has a density near 1.2 kg/m³.

records.stem: A 5 kg body accelerates at 10 m/s². What resultant force acts on it?
records.explanation: Newton’s second law gives F = ma = 5 × 10 = 50 N.

records.stem: What is the approximate density of mercury near room temperature?
records.explanation: Mercury’s density is approximately 13.6 g/cm³, or 13,600 kg/m³.

records.stem: Which is a scalar quantity?
records.explanation: Time has magnitude but no spatial direction.

records.stem: Where do paraxial rays parallel to a convex lens’s principal axis meet after refraction in air?
records.explanation: A converging lens brings paraxial parallel rays to its principal focus.

records.stem: What heat energy is generated by current I through resistance R in time t, with I and R constant?
records.explanation: Joule heating follows Q = power × time = I²Rt.

records.stem: A pump lifts 70 kg of water through 16 m in 10 s. Using g = 10 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W, what power is needed, approximately?
What is the SI unit of density?
records.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, so its unit is kg/m³.

records.stem: What is the bouncing back of sound at a boundary called?
records.explanation: Reflection sends sound back into the original medium; an audible delayed reflection is an echo.

records.stem: Which spherical mirror has a reflecting inner curved surface?
records.explanation: A concave mirror’s reflecting surface curves inward.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of surface tension?
records.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length along a liquid surface.

records.stem: A cat detects a 45,000 Hz sound. How is that frequency classified relative to ordinary human hearing?

options.label: C
options.text: Within the usual 20–20,000 Hz human range

records.explanation: 45,000 Hz exceeds the usual upper human hearing limit of 20,000 Hz.

records.stem: What is the approximate speed of sound in dry air at 0°C?
records.explanation: Sound travels in dry air at about 331 m/s at 0°C and faster at higher temperatures.

records.stem: If a diamond sample’s Young’s modulus is given as 1.12 × 10¹² Pa, what is it in GPa?
records.explanation: Since 1 GPa = 10⁹ Pa, the stated modulus equals 1,120 GPa.

records.stem: A stone has mass 500 g and volume 20 cm³. What is its density?
records.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 500/20 = 25 g/cm³; the source’s options omitted the correct value.

records.stem: How is Celsius temperature C converted to Fahrenheit temperature F?
records.explanation: The Fahrenheit scale uses an interval factor of 9/5 and a 32-degree offset.

records.stem: What representative thermal conductivity for ice is listed in OpenStax’s College Physics table?
records.explanation: The cited table gives ice a representative thermal conductivity of 2.2 W/(m·K).

records.stem: Which two mechanisms chiefly transfer heat from a room heater to the room and its occupants?
records.explanation: Air circulates by convection while a hot heater also emits thermal radiation.

records.stem: What representative thermal-conductivity range for wood is listed in OpenStax’s College Physics table?
records.explanation: The cited table gives a range, since wood type, moisture and grain affect conductivity.

records.stem: Where does a paraxial ray parallel to a concave mirror’s principal axis pass after reflection?
records.explanation: For a concave mirror, a parallel paraxial ray reflects through the principal focus.

records.stem: Which waves require a material medium for propagation?
records.explanation: Mechanical waves are disturbances of matter and cannot propagate in a vacuum.

records.stem: What energy does elevated water stored behind a dam possess because of its height?
records.explanation: Its height in Earth’s gravitational field gives the water gravitational potential energy.

records.stem: What is the approximate temperature of the Sun’s core?
records.explanation: The Sun’s core reaches roughly 15 million degrees, enabling nuclear fusion.

records.stem: Which sound characteristic distinguishes a high, shrill note from a low, deep note?
records.explanation: Pitch depends mainly on sound frequency.

records.stem: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
records.explanation: Electric current measures charge flow per unit time and uses amperes.

records.stem: What is the approximate electric charge of a proton?
records.explanation: A proton carries one positive elementary charge.

records.stem: A mosquito’s buzzing is measured at 30 dB relative to intensity I₀. What is I/I₀?
records.explanation: From L = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀), 30 dB gives an intensity ratio of 10³.

records.stem: Treating carbon dioxide as an ideal gas at 273 K and constant pressure, what is its volume-expansion coefficient β, approximately?
records.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant pressure, β = 1/T = 1/273 ≈ 3.66 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹.

records.stem: Why was mercury historically useful in liquid-in-glass thermometers?

options.label: A
options.text: It is completely harmless if spilled

options.label: B
options.text: It expands relatively regularly and does not readily wet glass

options.label: D
options.text: It freezes at ordinary room temperature

records.explanation: Mercury’s visible column and relatively regular expansion supported thermometer use, although it is toxic.

records.stem: What type of waves is commonly studied using a ripple tank?
records.explanation: A ripple tank makes surface-water wave patterns visible for studying reflection and other behaviours.

records.stem: Which device commonly uses a concave mirror to form a strong directed beam?
records.explanation: A light source near a concave mirror’s focus produces a nearly parallel reflected beam.

records.stem: Using v = 331√(T/273) m/s for dry air, what is sound speed at 100°C, approximately?
records.explanation: Substituting T = 373 K gives 331√(373/273) ≈ 387 m/s.

records.stem: What is the gravitational force exerted by Earth on a body called?
records.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body.

records.stem: What provides the tangential restoring force of an ideal simple pendulum?

options.label: C
options.text: The tangential component of its weight

records.explanation: Gravity contributes the restoring component −mg sin θ; tension acts along the string.

records.stem: What is the approximate electric charge of an electron?
records.explanation: An electron carries one negative elementary charge; the source omitted the sign and unit.

records.stem: Which spherical mirror has a reflecting outer curved surface?
records.explanation: A convex mirror’s reflecting surface curves outward.

records.stem: What is tan 30°?
What waves have medium-particle vibrations perpendicular to the direction of propagation?
records.explanation: Perpendicular oscillation defines a transverse wave.

records.stem: Among typical solids, liquids and gases, in which does sound generally travel fastest?
records.explanation: Typical solids’ high stiffness produces higher sound speeds than liquids or gases, though material properties matter.

records.stem: Rustling leaves are measured at 10 dB relative to intensity I₀. What is I/I₀?
records.explanation: A level of 10 dB gives 10 log₁₀(I/I₀) = 10, hence I/I₀ = 10.

records.stem: What is the approximate rest mass of an electron?
records.explanation: An electron’s rest mass is approximately 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kilograms.

records.stem: Using the ideal-gas approximation v = √(γRT/M), γ = 1.4 and M = 0.002 kg/mol, what is sound speed in hydrogen at 273 K, approximately?
A constant 40 N force moves its point of application 1 m in the force’s direction. What work is done?
records.explanation: Work W = Fs = 40 × 1 = 40 J under the specified parallel condition.

records.stem: What is charge separation in an insulated conductor caused by a nearby charged body called?
records.explanation: A nearby electric field redistributes the conductor’s charges without requiring contact.

records.stem: What is the approximate refractive index of ethanol for visible light near room temperature?
records.explanation: Ethanol’s refractive index is approximately 1.36 and varies with wavelength and temperature.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of volume?
records.explanation: Volume has three dimensions of length, giving m³.

records.stem: Which power of ten is represented by the SI prefix mega?
records.explanation: Mega means one million, or 10⁶.

records.stem: What are oscillations whose amplitude decreases because of resistive effects called?
records.explanation: Damping removes mechanical energy and decreases oscillation amplitude.

records.stem: In simple harmonic motion, how is acceleration related to displacement x from equilibrium?
records.explanation: Acceleration is proportional to displacement in magnitude and directed back towards equilibrium.

records.stem: Approximately how many elementary-charge magnitudes equal 1 coulomb?
records.explanation: Dividing 1 C by 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives approximately 6.24 × 10¹⁸ charges.

records.stem: What is the area of a circle of radius r?
records.explanation: A circle’s area is π times the square of its radius.

records.stem: What is the critical angle for light going from glass of refractive index 1.50 into air of index 1.00, approximately?
records.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/1.5 gives c ≈ 41.8°, so the index must be specified.

records.stem: Which ordinary lens in air converges paraxial rays parallel to its principal axis?
records.explanation: A convex lens in air focuses parallel rays to its principal focus.

records.stem: A car weighs 12 kN and moves at 20 m/s. Using g = 10 m/s², what is its kinetic energy?
What is the approximate gravitational acceleration on the Moon?
records.explanation: The Moon’s surface gravitational acceleration is approximately 1.62 m/s².

records.stem: What are mercury’s approximate freezing and boiling points at 1 atm?
records.explanation: Mercury freezes near −38.8°C and boils near 356.7°C at atmospheric pressure.

records.stem: What is the approximate universal molar gas constant R?
records.explanation: R is the molar constant in PV = nRT, not a gas-specific constant per kilogram.

records.stem: Which is a nonrenewable energy source?
records.explanation: Fossil fuels form over geological timescales and are not replenished at the rate of consumption.

records.stem: What is sin²θ + cos²θ for any real angle θ?
records.explanation: The Pythagorean trigonometric identity gives sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

records.stem: What is the approximate rest mass of a neutron?
records.explanation: A neutron’s mass is approximately 1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kilograms.

records.stem: What is the ratio of image height to object height called?
records.explanation: Linear magnification compares the image’s linear size with that of the object.

records.stem: A bat emits a 120,000 Hz call. How is that frequency classified relative to ordinary human hearing?

options.label: A
options.text: Within the usual 20–20,000 Hz human range

records.explanation: 120,000 Hz is above ordinary human hearing; no universal hearing limit for all bats is assumed.

records.stem: What is fuel derived from plant or animal organic material called?
records.explanation: Biomass is organic material used as fuel or converted into usable fuel.

records.stem: For a paraxial spherical mirror of radius of curvature R, what is the focal-length magnitude?
records.explanation: A spherical mirror’s paraxial focal length has magnitude half its curvature radius.

records.stem: What energy is stored in coal’s chemical structure?
records.explanation: Combustion releases energy from chemical reactions involving coal.

records.stem: For a stretched rubber balloon in static equilibrium, how does its internal pressure usually compare with external pressure?

options.label: D
options.text: It is equal for every stretched balloon

records.explanation: Excess internal pressure balances the tension in the stretched rubber membrane.

records.stem: How many colour bands are traditionally named in the visible spectrum of white light?
records.explanation: The conventional seven-colour description names red through violet, although the spectrum is continuous.

records.stem: A convex lens has power +100 dioptres. What is its focal length?
records.explanation: P = 1/f with f in metres gives f = 1/100 = 0.01 m.

records.stem: What representative linear-expansion coefficient for copper is listed by OpenStax, approximately?
records.explanation: The cited table gives copper α = 17 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.

records.stem: What is the conventional approximate normal human body temperature?
records.explanation: 37°C is the conventional reference value, though actual readings vary with person and measurement site.

records.stem: If a tyre-road contact is assigned μ = 0.40 and normal force 1,000 N, what maximum static friction does that model predict?
records.explanation: With the coefficient explicitly given, limiting friction is μN = 400 N.

records.stem: For an isotropic solid with linear-expansion coefficient α = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, what is β approximately?
records.explanation: For small expansion of an isotropic solid, β ≈ 3α.

records.stem: In E = mc², what does c represent?

options.label: D
options.text: Speed of an electron in every atom

records.explanation: c is the invariant vacuum speed of light, approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

records.stem: Water waves have frequency 12 Hz and wavelength 3 cm. What is their speed?
What is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature?
records.explanation: Thermodynamic temperature is measured in kelvins.

records.stem: For light entering a medium from air with index approximately 1, what is its refractive index n in terms of incidence i and refraction r?
records.explanation: Snell’s law with incident index 1 gives n = sin i/sin r.

records.stem: What is the time taken to complete one oscillation called?
records.explanation: The period T is the duration of one complete cycle.

records.stem: A longitudinal sound wave is assigned speed 5,950 m/s in an iron sample. How far does it travel in 0.10 s?
records.explanation: Using the stated sample speed, distance = vt = 5,950 × 0.10 = 595 m.

records.stem: For equal volumes near room temperature, which listed substance has the lowest mass?
records.explanation: Equal-volume mass is proportional to density, and aluminium has the lowest density among these choices.

records.stem: Which surface is generally a good emitter of thermal radiation?
records.explanation: Dull black surfaces generally have higher emissivity than polished metallic surfaces.

records.stem: What is the critical angle for light travelling from water of index 1.33 into air of index 1.00, approximately?
records.explanation: sin c = 1/1.33 gives a critical angle near 48.8°.

records.stem: Oil and natural gas mainly consist of compounds made from which two elements?
records.explanation: Oil and natural gas are predominantly hydrocarbons; coal is not simply a pure hydrocarbon.

records.stem: What type of energy is stored in a stretched spring?
records.explanation: Stretching a spring stores recoverable elastic potential energy.

records.stem: What is the boiling point of mercury?
records.explanation: Mercury boils near 356.7°C at atmospheric pressure.

records.stem: What is the traditional steam-point temperature of pure water at 1 atm on the Fahrenheit scale?
records.explanation: The traditional steam point of pure water at 1 atm is 212°F.

records.stem: Mercury is used as a thermometric material because it has:

options.label: B
options.text: A very high specific heat capacity

options.label: C
options.text: A high freezing point and large heat capacity

options.label: D
options.text: A low freezing point, small heat capacity, and uniform thermal expansion

records.explanation: Mercury’s physical properties historically made a visible expanding thermometer column useful.

records.stem: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K is called:
records.explanation: Specific heat capacity is heat per unit mass per unit temperature increase.

records.stem: What is the traditional steam-point temperature of pure water at 1 atm on the Kelvin temperature scale?
records.explanation: The traditional steam point is 373.15 K, rounded to 373 K; it is not a modern definition of the kelvin.

records.stem: Splitting a vector into two components is called:
records.explanation: Vector resolution expresses one vector as components along chosen directions.

records.stem: The force directly proportional to the product of two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them is described by:
records.explanation: Newton’s universal gravitation law relates force to two masses and their separation squared.

records.stem: A zero between two significant figures is also called:
records.explanation: A captive zero lies between nonzero digits and is significant.

records.stem: A falling raindrop has reached terminal speed. What is its subsequent velocity while conditions remain unchanged?
records.explanation: At terminal speed, upward drag balances weight and acceleration is zero.

records.stem: What is the approximate mass of the Earth?
records.explanation: Earth’s mass is approximately 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg.

records.stem: What is the formula for work done when force and displacement are in the same direction?
records.explanation: For a parallel constant force, work equals force times displacement.

records.stem: Which law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction?
records.explanation: Newton’s third law states that interaction forces on different bodies are equal and opposite.

records.stem: Who described the relationship between mass and energy?
records.explanation: Einstein established mass–energy equivalence, expressed as E = mc².

records.stem: What is the process by which heat is transferred through a fluid?
records.explanation: Convection transfers heat through the bulk movement of a fluid.

records.stem: What is the degree of the nonzero constant polynomial p(x) = a, where a ≠ 0?
records.explanation: A nonzero constant polynomial has highest power x⁰ and therefore degree zero.

records.stem: What is the general form of a linear equation in one variable x, with a ≠ 0?
records.explanation: With nonzero coefficient a, the highest power of x is one.

records.stem: Newton's First Law of Motion is also called:
records.explanation: Newton’s first law describes the persistence of rest or uniform motion without resultant force.

records.stem: What is power?

options.label: A
options.text: The energy stored in a body

options.label: B
options.text: The force acting on a body

options.label: D
options.text: The distance travelled by a body

records.explanation: Power measures energy transferred or work done per unit time.

records.stem: One watt is equal to:
records.explanation: One watt equals one joule transferred per second.

records.stem: Sound waves in air are which type of waves?
records.explanation: Air particles vibrate parallel to sound propagation in longitudinal waves.

records.stem: Which rays have the highest ionizing power among alpha, beta, and gamma rays?
records.explanation: Alpha particles have high ionizing power but relatively low penetrating power.

records.stem: What is electrical resistance?

options.label: A
options.text: The potential difference across a circuit

options.label: B
options.text: The opposition to the flow of electric current

options.label: C
options.text: The rate of flow of charge

options.label: D
options.text: The energy stored in a battery

records.explanation: Resistance describes how strongly a conductor opposes current for a given potential difference.

records.stem: For two nonzero vectors making an acute angle θ, when do their dot-product magnitude and cross-product magnitude match?
records.explanation: Within 0° < θ < 90°, equality requires cos θ = sin θ, giving 45°.

records.stem: What is the perfect-square form of x² + 64x + 1024?
records.explanation: Since 64 = 2 × 32 and 1024 = 32², the expression equals (x + 32)².

records.stem: Into how many parts does a midpoint cut a line segment?
records.explanation: A midpoint divides a segment into two equal lengths.

records.stem: If the input energy is 100 units and the output energy is 3 units, what is the efficiency?
records.explanation: Efficiency = useful output/input × 100% = 3/100 × 100% = 3%.

records.stem: In which state of matter do particles generally vibrate about fixed positions?
records.explanation: In a typical solid, particles oscillate around equilibrium positions.

records.stem: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
records.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to speed squared, so doubling speed multiplies it by four.

records.stem: Which force keeps a body moving in a circular path?
records.explanation: Circular motion needs a resultant force directed towards the centre.

records.stem: The spinning motion of a body around its own axis is called:
records.explanation: Rotation is motion about an axis.

records.stem: What is the formula for efficiency?
records.explanation: Efficiency is useful output energy divided by total input energy, multiplied by 100%.

records.stem: Which of the following is a poor conductor of heat?
records.explanation: Wood has much lower thermal conductivity than the listed metals.

records.stem: A rocket is an example of which of Newton's laws of motion?
records.explanation: A rocket accelerates as expelled gases and the rocket exert equal opposite forces.

records.stem: What is Newton's Second Law of Motion expressed mathematically?
records.explanation: For constant mass, Newton’s second law is F = ma.

records.stem: What is the approximate thermal conductivity of air at room temperature?
records.explanation: Dry air near 20°C has thermal conductivity approximately 0.026 W/(m·K), varying with temperature.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of heat?
records.explanation: Heat is transferred energy and its SI unit is the joule.

records.stem: What is the approximate value of Boltzmann's constant?
records.explanation: Boltzmann’s constant connects temperature with molecular energy and is about 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K.

records.stem: Which formula expresses inductive reactance in terms of frequency f and inductance L?
records.explanation: For an ideal inductor in sinusoidal AC, reactance is angular frequency times inductance.

records.stem: Which law states that stress is proportional to strain within the linear elastic region?
records.explanation: Hooke’s law describes the proportional stress–strain relationship in the linear elastic region.

records.stem: Who discovered nitrogen?
records.explanation: Daniel Rutherford identified nitrogen in 1772.

records.stem: Which deficiency can reduce haemoglobin production and cause a common nutritional anaemia?
records.explanation: Iron deficiency can limit haemoglobin production and cause iron-deficiency anaemia.

records.stem: What is the approximate value of Planck's constant?
records.explanation: Planck’s constant is approximately 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

records.stem: What is one light-year approximately equal to?
records.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in a Julian year, about 9.46 × 10¹⁵ metres.

records.stem: What resting pulse range is commonly considered normal for most adults?
records.explanation: The American Heart Association gives 60–100 beats per minute for most adults, with exceptions such as trained athletes.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
records.explanation: Force is measured in newtons, equivalent to kg·m/s².

records.stem: What is the approximate acceleration due to gravity on Earth?
records.explanation: The conventional approximate near-surface Earth value of g is 9.8 m/s².

records.stem: Which physical quantity is defined as the rate of change of displacement?
records.explanation: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement.

records.stem: For a body moving with constant velocity, what remains unchanged about its velocity?

options.label: A
options.text: Its speed only, with changing direction

options.label: B
options.text: Its direction only, with changing speed

records.explanation: Velocity is constant only when both its magnitude and direction remain constant.

records.stem: What is the formula for momentum?
records.explanation: Momentum equals mass times velocity.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of momentum?
records.explanation: The momentum unit follows p = mv, giving kg·m/s.

records.stem: Which law explains why passengers move forward when a moving bus suddenly stops?
records.explanation: Inertia causes a passenger’s body to continue moving when the bus slows.

records.stem: What is the formula for average speed?
records.explanation: Average speed is total path distance divided by total elapsed time.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of work?
records.explanation: Work is transferred energy measured in joules.

records.stem: When is work done by a force zero?
records.explanation: Work W = F·s is zero when displacement is zero.

records.stem: Which energy does a moving body possess?
records.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy associated with motion.

records.stem: One horsepower is approximately equal to:
records.explanation: One mechanical horsepower is approximately 746 watts.

records.stem: What is the formula for mechanical advantage?
records.explanation: Mechanical advantage compares the output load force to the input effort force.

records.stem: What property describes resistance to a change in velocity?
records.explanation: Inertia is an object’s resistance to changes in its state of motion.

records.stem: A body has mass 5 kg on Earth. Neglecting any loss of material, what is its mass on the Moon?
records.explanation: Changing gravitational field changes weight, not the body’s mass.

records.stem: Which quantity is a scalar?
records.explanation: Speed is magnitude without direction and is therefore scalar.

records.stem: What is the resultant of two equal and opposite forces acting along the same line?
records.explanation: Equal opposite collinear forces cancel vectorially.

records.stem: What is the formula for density?
records.explanation: Density is the mass contained in each unit of volume.

records.stem: Which principle explains the operation of hydraulic machines?
records.explanation: Pascal’s principle transmits pressure changes throughout an enclosed fluid.

records.stem: At what temperature does pure water freeze on the Celsius scale at standard atmospheric pressure?
records.explanation: Pure water freezes near 0°C at standard atmospheric pressure.

records.stem: At what temperature does pure water boil on the Celsius scale at standard atmospheric pressure?
records.explanation: Pure water boils near 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure.

records.stem: What is the approximate value of absolute zero in Celsius?
records.explanation: Absolute zero is 0 K, equivalent to −273.15°C.

records.stem: Which instrument measures temperature?
records.explanation: A thermometer indicates temperature.

records.stem: Which mode of heat transfer can occur through a vacuum?
records.explanation: Electromagnetic thermal radiation can propagate through a vacuum.

records.stem: Heat transfer through direct contact between particles is called:
records.explanation: Conduction transfers heat through microscopic interactions without bulk fluid transport.

records.stem: Which material is generally a good conductor of heat?
records.explanation: Copper conducts heat efficiently because of its mobile electrons and material structure.

records.stem: Which material is commonly used as a thermal insulator?
records.explanation: Fibreglass traps air and reduces heat conduction.

records.stem: What is the formula for heat absorbed when a substance changes temperature without changing state?
records.explanation: With no phase change, Q = mcΔT relates heat to mass, specific heat and temperature change.

records.stem: For a pure substance undergoing a phase transition at constant pressure, what is latent heat?

options.label: A
options.text: Energy absorbed or released during the transition without a temperature change

records.explanation: During the transition, energy changes the phase rather than the temperature under the stated conditions.

records.stem: What is the change of state from liquid to gas called?
records.explanation: Vaporization is the transition from liquid to gas.

records.stem: What is the change of state from gas to liquid called?
records.explanation: Condensation is the transition from gas to liquid.

records.stem: Why does evaporation cause cooling?

options.label: A
options.text: The liquid gains heat from the surroundings

options.label: D
options.text: Higher-energy molecules escape from the liquid

records.explanation: Escaping molecules carry away energy, lowering the average energy of those remaining.

records.stem: Which scale has its zero at absolute zero?
records.explanation: The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero.

records.stem: What is the approximate normal human body temperature in Fahrenheit?
records.explanation: 37°C converts to 98.6°F using F = (9/5)C + 32.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
records.explanation: Specific heat is energy per unit mass per unit temperature rise.

records.stem: Which metal is commonly used in liquid-in-glass thermometers because it expands relatively uniformly with temperature?
records.explanation: Mercury’s relatively regular thermal expansion historically supported thermometer use.

records.stem: What happens to most substances when they are heated?
records.explanation: Most substances expand when heated, although exceptions such as water near freezing exist.

records.stem: Which law relates the pressure and volume of a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature?
records.explanation: Boyle’s law keeps PV constant for fixed gas amount at constant temperature.

records.stem: What is the approximate speed of sound in dry air at 20°C?
records.explanation: Sound speed in dry air at 20°C is approximately 343 m/s.

records.stem: Can sound travel through a vacuum?

options.label: B
options.text: No, it requires a material medium

records.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs matter to carry its disturbance.

records.stem: Which property of sound determines its pitch?
records.explanation: Higher sound frequency corresponds to higher pitch.

records.stem: Which property of a sound wave is mainly associated with its loudness?
records.explanation: Greater amplitude generally corresponds to greater sound intensity and perceived loudness.

records.stem: What is the relationship between frequency and time period?
records.explanation: Frequency and period are reciprocals, so f = 1/T.

records.stem: What is the approximate frequency range of human hearing?
records.explanation: The often-quoted young-human hearing range is about 20 Hz to 20 kHz and narrows with age.

records.stem: Sound with a frequency above 20,000 Hz is called:
records.explanation: Ultrasound has frequency above the conventional 20 kHz human hearing limit.

records.stem: Sound with a frequency below 20 Hz is called:
records.explanation: Infrasound has frequency below the conventional 20 Hz lower hearing limit.

records.stem: What is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another called?
records.explanation: Refraction occurs when light changes speed and usually direction between media.

records.stem: What is the bouncing back of light from a surface called?
records.explanation: Reflection sends light back from a boundary.

records.stem: Which mirror gives an upright magnified shaving image when the face is within its focal length?
records.explanation: A concave mirror forms an upright enlarged virtual image when the object is inside its focal length.

records.stem: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
records.explanation: The vacuum speed of light is exactly 299,792,458 m/s, approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

records.stem: Which electromagnetic radiation has the longest wavelength among the following?
records.explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths among these listed electromagnetic categories.

records.stem: Which electromagnetic radiation has the highest frequency?
records.explanation: Gamma rays occupy the highest-frequency end of the conventional electromagnetic spectrum.

records.stem: What is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours called?
records.explanation: Dispersion separates colours because refractive index varies with wavelength.

records.stem: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
records.explanation: Red occupies the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum.

records.stem: Which colour of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
records.explanation: Violet occupies the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum.

records.stem: What is the SI unit of potential difference?
records.explanation: Potential difference is energy per charge and is measured in volts.

records.stem: Which instrument measures electric current?
records.explanation: An ammeter measures current and is normally connected in series.

records.stem: Which instrument measures potential difference?
records.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference between two points.

records.stem: What happens to the total resistance when resistors are connected in series?

options.label: A
options.text: Total resistance is always less than the smallest resistance

options.label: B
options.text: Resistance becomes infinite in every case

records.explanation: Series resistors carry the same current and their voltage drops add, so their resistances add.

records.stem: In a parallel circuit, the potential difference across each branch is:
records.explanation: Parallel branches share the same two connection points and therefore the same potential difference.

records.stem: What is the formula for electrical power?
records.explanation: Electrical power equals potential difference multiplied by current.

records.stem: Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
records.explanation: An electric motor uses electromagnetic forces to produce mechanical motion.

records.stem: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
records.explanation: A generator converts mechanical motion into electrical energy by induction.

records.stem: What is the function of a fuse in an electrical circuit?

options.label: B
options.text: To protect the circuit from excessive current

records.explanation: A fuse melts when excessive current heats its element, opening the circuit.

records.stem: Which particles carry electric current in a metal wire?
records.explanation: Mobile electrons carry current through an ordinary metal conductor.

records.stem: Which material is strongly attracted to a magnet?
records.explanation: Iron is ferromagnetic and can be strongly attracted by a magnet.

records.stem: What happens when two like magnetic poles are brought together?
records.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel while unlike poles attract.

records.stem: Which particle has a negative electric charge?
records.explanation: An electron has a negative elementary charge.

records.stem: Which particle has no electric charge?
records.explanation: A neutron has zero net electric charge.

records.stem: Which radiation consists of helium nuclei?
records.explanation: An alpha particle contains two protons and two neutrons, like a helium-4 nucleus.

records.stem: Which equation expresses the equivalence of mass and energy?
records.explanation: Einstein’s E = mc² relates mass to its equivalent rest energy.

records.stem: In which quadrant does (−15, −9) lie?
records.explanation: Both coordinates are negative, placing the point in the third quadrant.

records.stem: What joins a triangle’s vertex to the midpoint of its opposite side?
records.explanation: A median connects a vertex with the opposite side’s midpoint.

records.stem: What is the radicand in ∛35?
records.explanation: The radicand is the quantity inside the radical sign.

records.stem: Write the seventh root of x in exponential form.
records.explanation: An nth root corresponds to the exponent 1/n.

records.stem: Write 4^(2/3) using a radical.
records.explanation: The denominator 3 gives the root index and numerator 2 gives the power.

records.stem: What is an equation with a variable under a radical sign called?
records.explanation: A radical equation contains its unknown within a radical expression.

records.stem: In the nth root of a, what is a called?
records.explanation: The radicand is the expression whose root is being taken.

records.stem: If x : y = z : z, with y ≠ 0 and z ≠ 0, what follows?
records.explanation: Since z/z = 1, x/y = 1 implies x = y.

records.stem: If 5 kg of apples cost Rs. 250, what do 16 kg cost at the same rate?
records.explanation: The unit price is 250/5 = Rs. 50 per kg, so 16 kg cost Rs. 800.

records.stem: Every real number can also be regarded as which kind of number?
records.explanation: A real number r is the complex number r + 0i.

records.stem: What is log_b(1), for b > 0 and b ≠ 1?
records.explanation: Since b⁰ = 1, its logarithm is zero.

records.stem: Who published A Memoir on the Theory of Matrices in 1858?
records.explanation: Cayley developed matrix theory in that memoir; Sylvester had introduced the term “matrix”.

records.stem: What is a vertical arrangement of entries in a matrix called?
records.explanation: A column runs vertically, while a row runs horizontally.

records.stem: If the matrix [[3, 6], [x, 8]] is singular, what is x?
records.explanation: Its determinant 24 − 6x must be zero, giving x = 4.

records.stem: For real a and b, what is the real part of 2ab(i + i²)?
records.explanation: Since i² = −1, the expression is −2ab + 2abi.

records.stem: Simplify √3(2√3 + 3√3).
records.explanation: The bracket is 5√3, so multiplying by √3 gives 5 × 3 = 15.

records.stem: What is a matrix with equal numbers of rows and columns called?
records.explanation: A square matrix has order n × n.

records.stem: If x − a is a factor of P(x), what is the remainder on division by x − a?
records.explanation: The factor theorem gives P(a) = 0 when x − a is a factor.

records.stem: In traditional common-logarithm notation, what is the integer part called?
records.explanation: The characteristic supplies the integer part, with the fractional part recorded as the mantissa.

records.stem: Factorize a² − b².
records.explanation: The difference-of-squares identity gives a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

records.stem: What term completes 9a² − 12ab to the square (3a − 2b)²?
records.explanation: Expanding (3a − 2b)² gives 9a² − 12ab + 4b².

records.stem: Using the convention that natural numbers start at 1, what is {1, 2, 3, …}?
records.explanation: Under the stated convention, natural numbers are the positive counting numbers.

records.stem: What is the polynomial LCM of a² + b² and a⁴ − b⁴?
records.explanation: Since a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² + b²)(a² − b²), the first polynomial divides the second.

records.stem: What is the monic polynomial HCF of x − 2 and x² + x − 6?
records.explanation: The second polynomial factors as (x − 2)(x + 3).

records.stem: What term completes x⁴ + 64 to the square (x² + 8)²?
records.explanation: Expanding gives (x² + 8)² = x⁴ + 16x² + 64.

records.stem: Which order describes a square matrix?
records.explanation: Only 2 × 2 has equal numbers of rows and columns.

records.stem: Which line is parallel to the x-axis?
records.explanation: A constant-y line is horizontal and parallel to the x-axis.

records.stem: What percentage is 1,023 marks out of 1,100?
What is the usual notation for the transpose of matrix A?
records.explanation: Aᵀ denotes the matrix obtained by interchanging rows and columns.

records.stem: What is {0, 1, 2, 3, …} conventionally called in school arithmetic?
records.explanation: Whole numbers comprise zero and the positive counting numbers.

records.stem: For cos θ ≠ 0, what is tan θ?
records.explanation: Tangent is defined as sine divided by cosine.

records.stem: Who published the first influential work introducing logarithms in 1614?
records.explanation: Napier’s 1614 publication introduced logarithms as a practical calculating tool.

records.stem: What is the common antilogarithm of x?
records.explanation: The common antilogarithm reverses base-10 logarithms through exponentiation.

records.stem: What is the HCF of 5x²y² and 20x³y³?
records.explanation: Take the coefficient HCF 5 and the smallest exponent of each variable.

records.stem: Factorize a³ + b³.
records.explanation: The sum-of-cubes identity has the factors a + b and a² − ab + b².

records.stem: What is the total degree of 4x³ + 7x²y³ + 3?
records.explanation: The term x²y³ has total degree 2 + 3 = 5, the largest term degree.

records.stem: What is the leading coefficient of 3x² + 8x + 5?
records.explanation: The highest-power term is 3x², whose coefficient is 3.
Integers include negative whole numbers, zero and positive whole numbers.

records.stem: What is the fractional part in traditional common-logarithm tables called?
records.explanation: The fractional part is the mantissa, distinguished from the integer characteristic.

records.stem: In which quadrant does (−3, −3) lie?
records.explanation: Both coordinates are negative, so the point lies in the third quadrant.

records.stem: If P(x) = 4x³ − 4x + 3, what is P(1)?
records.explanation: Substitution gives 4 − 4 + 3 = 3.

records.stem: What is the distance between (0, 0) and (1, 1)?
records.explanation: The distance formula gives √[(1 − 0)² + (1 − 0)²] = √2.

records.stem: Write 6.35 × 10⁶ in ordinary decimal notation.
records.explanation: Multiplication by 10⁶ shifts the decimal point six places right.

records.stem: What is a number written as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ abs(a) < 10 and n is an integer, said to use?
records.explanation: Scientific notation uses a normalized coefficient multiplied by a power of ten.

records.stem: What is a triangle with exactly two equal sides called?
records.explanation: Two equal sides define an isosceles triangle; “exactly” excludes equilateral here.

records.stem: What is a triangle with all three sides of different lengths called?
records.explanation: A scalene triangle has no equal sides.

records.stem: What is the monic polynomial HCF of a² − b² and a³ − b³?
records.explanation: Their factorizations share a − b but not the remaining factors.

records.stem: Multiply the row matrix [x, y] by the column matrix [[2], [−1]].
records.explanation: The row–column product is x × 2 + y × (−1), a 1 × 1 matrix.

records.stem: If x = log_b(y), with b > 0, b ≠ 1 and y > 0, what is y relative to x?
records.explanation: The equivalent exponential form is y = b^x.

records.stem: For p, q > 0, simplify log_b(p/q), where b > 0 and b ≠ 1.
records.explanation: The logarithm quotient rule turns division into subtraction.

records.stem: What is the set {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …}?
records.explanation: Primes are integers greater than one with exactly two positive divisors; 1 was removed from the source.

records.stem: For positive integers A and B, A × B equals which expression?
records.explanation: Each prime’s minimum and maximum exponents together equal its exponents in the product.

records.stem: What is the LCM of 15x², 45xy and 30xyz?
records.explanation: The coefficient LCM is 90 and the largest powers are x², y and z.

records.stem: For sin θ ≠ 0, what is cot θ?
records.explanation: Cotangent is cosine divided by sine.

records.stem: In a polynomial in x, what exponents of x are permitted?
records.explanation: Polynomial exponents must be whole-number powers including zero.

records.stem: What is the monic HCF of x² + 3x + 2, x² + 4x + 3 and x² + 5x + 4?
records.explanation: The three factorizations are (x + 1)(x + 2), (x + 1)(x + 3) and (x + 1)(x + 4).

records.stem: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 30°. What is its vertex angle?
records.explanation: The two base angles are equal, so the vertex angle is 180° − 60° = 120°.
Equal matrices have equal corresponding entries, giving a = 3.

records.stem: If 5 kg of apples cost Rs. 200, what do 12 kg cost at the same rate?
records.explanation: The unit price is Rs. 40 per kg, so 12 kg cost Rs. 480.

records.stem: What is the complex conjugate of 5 + 4i?
records.explanation: Complex conjugation changes the sign of the imaginary part only.

records.stem: What is cos²θ equal to?
records.explanation: Rearranging sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 gives cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ.

records.stem: For m > 0 and a valid logarithm base b, simplify log_b(m^n).
records.explanation: The logarithm power rule brings the exponent n outside as a multiplier.

records.stem: What is the imaginary part of (−1 + √2)², interpreted literally?
records.explanation: The expression contains only real numbers, so its imaginary part is zero.

records.stem: What is the set {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, …}?
records.explanation: These are the positive integers divisible by two.

records.stem: Joining all three side midpoints of a triangle forms how many mutually congruent smaller triangles?
records.explanation: The midpoint theorem gives four triangles with corresponding sides half those of the original.

records.stem: What is the base of the modern natural logarithm ln x?
records.explanation: The natural logarithm is defined to base e; this avoids equating it with Napier’s original historical construction.

records.stem: What is the root index of the seventh root of x?
records.explanation: The radical index states which root is being taken.

records.stem: What is the polynomial HCF of a³ + b³ and a² − ab + b²?
records.explanation: The cubic equals (a + b)(a² − ab + b²), so the quadratic divides it.

records.stem: If a positive number’s common logarithm has characteristic 1, how many digits are in its integer part?
records.explanation: A characteristic of 1 means 10 ≤ number < 100, giving two integer digits.

records.stem: What is i¹⁰, where i² = −1?
records.explanation: Powers of i repeat every four, and i¹⁰ = i² = −1.

records.stem: If x ≠ 0 and x + 1/x = 3, what is x³ + 1/x³?
records.explanation: Using a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b) gives 27 − 9 = 18.

records.stem: Which pair names two common school methods for finding an HCF?
records.explanation: Factorisation compares common prime powers, while repeated division uses the Euclidean algorithm.

records.stem: Which inequality is satisfied by x = 0?
records.explanation: Substituting zero gives −2 < 0 only in the keyed option.

records.stem: Which ordered pair lies on y = x?
records.explanation: Points on y = x have equal coordinates.

records.stem: What is sin²θ equal to?
records.explanation: Rearranging the Pythagorean identity gives sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ.

records.stem: If θ is acute and tan θ = √3, what is θ?
records.explanation: The standard value tan 60° = √3 gives the unique acute solution.

records.stem: In traditional logarithm-table notation, a common logarithm is written −3 + 0.3705. What is its mantissa?
records.explanation: The positive fractional part 0.3705 is the mantissa; the negative characteristic is recorded separately.

records.stem: How are square roots of positive nonsquare integers classified?
records.explanation: A positive integer has a rational square root only when it is a perfect square.

records.stem: Which definition correctly describes a polynomial in one variable?

options.label: A
options.text: Any expression containing a radical variable

options.label: B
options.text: A finite sum of terms c_k x^k with nonnegative integer k

options.label: C
options.text: An expression with exactly one term

options.label: D
options.text: An expression with exactly two terms

records.explanation: A polynomial can have any finite number of terms, including one, with nonnegative integer exponents.

records.stem: For a, b ≥ 0, simplify (√a + √b)(√a − √b).
records.explanation: The difference-of-squares identity gives (√a)² − (√b)² = a − b.

records.stem: Which radical evaluates to a rational number and is therefore not an irrational surd?
records.explanation: √25 = 5 is rational, unlike the other square roots.

records.stem: Expand the supplied expression (2x + 3y)(4x² + 6xy + 9y²).
records.explanation: Distribution preserves the positive middle term and gives cross terms 24x²y and 36xy².

records.stem: If a + b = 3 and a − b = 4, what is a² + b²?
records.explanation: Adding the squared equations gives 2(a² + b²) = 9 + 16 = 25.

records.stem: What is the remainder when polynomial P(x) is divided by x − a?
records.explanation: The remainder theorem evaluates the remainder at the divisor’s root a.

records.stem: Reconstructed question: If x − 2 is a factor of P(x) = x² + kx + 8, what is k?
records.explanation: The factor theorem gives P(2) = 4 + 2k + 8 = 0, hence k = −6.

records.stem: What is the set {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, …}?
records.explanation: These are the positive integers not divisible by two.

records.stem: What are points lying on the same straight line called?
records.explanation: Collinearity means lying on a common straight line.

records.stem: What is the adjugate of [[1, 2], [0, −1]]?
records.explanation: For [[a,b],[c,d]], the adjugate is [[d,−b],[−c,a]].

records.stem: If P(x) = 6x⁴ + 2x³ − x + 2, what is P(0)?
records.explanation: At x = 0 all variable terms vanish, leaving the constant 2.

records.stem: For a ≠ b, simplify (a² − b²)/(a − b).
records.explanation: Factor the numerator as (a − b)(a + b) and cancel the nonzero denominator.

records.stem: What is the monic HCF of x² − 5x + 6 and x² − x − 6?
records.explanation: The factorizations (x − 2)(x − 3) and (x − 3)(x + 2) share x − 3.

records.stem: Which ordered pair satisfies y = 2x?
records.explanation: Substituting x = 1 gives y = 2.

records.stem: What percentage is 979 marks out of 1,100?
What is a triangle with three equal sides called?
records.explanation: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal.

records.stem: Which listed set is closed under addition?
records.explanation: Only {0} contains the sum of every pair of its own elements, since 0 + 0 = 0.

records.stem: What is the total degree of 4x² + 7x²y³ + 3?
records.explanation: The highest total degree is that of x²y³, equal to 2 + 3 = 5.

records.stem: What is the polynomial HCF of p³q − pq³ and p⁵q² − p²q⁵?
records.explanation: The factorizations pq(p − q)(p + q) and p²q²(p − q)(p² + pq + q²) share pq(p − q).
